## Before you start

Run the chunk below **once**. It creates a folder, `data/tx-housing-practice/`, with one CSV per year (2011–2014) of the `txhousing` data.

```{r make-files}
dir.create("data/tx-housing-practice", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
for (yr in 2011:2014) {
  txhousing |>
    filter(year == yr) |>
    write_csv(paste0("data/tx-housing-practice/txhousing_", yr, ".csv"))
}

files <- list.files("data/tx-housing-practice", pattern = "201[1-4]", full.names = TRUE)
files
```

Chunks containing `___` are set to `eval: false` so that this document still renders. When you fill in a chunk, delete its `#| eval: false` line.

### If you finish early: balanced A/B assignment by region

Marketing wants to test a new email design. They need **equal-sized groups within each region**, so that one group isn't mostly from the West, for example.

```{r}

  customer_id = 1:400,

)
```

## Practice 5: Bootstrap the 90th percentile

This uses the same audit sample as the slides:

```{r}
set.seed(7500)
audit <- diamonds |> slice_sample(n = 150)
```

**5a.** Build a 95% bootstrap percentile interval for the **median** price, as in the slides. Then build one for the **90th percentile** of price.

```{r}
#| eval: false
boot_median <- function(x) ___
boot_p90    <- function(x) ___

set.seed(7500)
medians <- replicate(5000, boot_median(audit$price))
p90s    <- replicate(5000, boot_p90(audit$price))

quantile(medians, c(0.025, 0.975))
quantile(p90s,    c(0.025, 0.975))
```

**5b.** Which interval is wider? Make a histogram of `price` in `audit` and use it to explain why.
